structuredIncident.summary: The R3 exit carrier beam fell from the yoke into the mill pit at approximately 1:03 PM on October 14, 2024 (Turn 2). The incident occurred during an outage preparation phase where work rolls and backup rolls had been removed. Key contextual facts include that the top backup roll balance was left isolated in a raised position and B hydraulics were shut off/bled prior to this shift's event. No team members were present in the pit at the time of impact, though witnesses observed it from outside.
structuredIncident.focalEvent: R3 exit carrier beam falls from yoke into mill pit
structuredIncident.actualImpact: Falling object (SIFp) with potential for death; no injuries reported as team was absent. Equipment damage not apparent on the link or keeper, though a small window liner fell.
structuredIncident.potentialImpact: Severe injury or fatality to personnel in the pit if present at time of failure; structural integrity loss requiring immediate area isolation (red-flagged).
structuredIncident.normalState: Operational roughing mill with carrier beam installed on yoke. Standard configuration includes work rolls and backup roll balances supporting system geometry.
structuredIncident.eventState: Outage preparation state: Work rolls removed, top/bottom backup rolls removed, R3 top backup roll balance isolated in raised position, B hydraulics shut off/bled. Beam fell from this specific configuration.

questions.text: Does the R3 carrier beam assembly rely on active hydraulic pressure from system 'B' (or another source) for retention when not mechanically locked?
questions.rationale: If yes, shutting off and bleeding B hydraulics creates an immediate failure mode. If no, this is a non-factor.
questions.decisionUnlocked: If yes, shutting off and bleeding B hydraulics creates an immediate failure mode. If no, this is a non-factor.

questions.text: Was the top backup roll balance physically locked/secured against gravity after being lifted, or did it rely solely on hydraulic pressure?
questions.rationale: If unsecured and reliant on hydraulics that were bled/shut off previously, this explains the fall. If mechanically secured, another cause is needed.
questions.decisionUnlocked: If unsecured and reliant on hydraulics that were bled/shut off previously, this explains the fall. If mechanically secured, another cause is needed.

questions.text: Were temporary mechanical supports (cribbing, stands) used to hold the top backup roll balance or carrier beam link during outage work?
questions.rationale: Absence of such supports combined with hydraulic shutdown could lead to uncontrolled descent. Presence suggests procedural compliance but potential failure in support design.
questions.decisionUnlocked: Absence of such supports combined with hydraulic shutdown could lead to uncontrolled descent. Presence suggests procedural compliance but potential failure in support design.

questions.text: Was a formal energy-isolation verification (zero-energy check) performed on the system supporting or adjacent to the carrier beam link?
questions.rationale: If isolation was incomplete or misinterpreted, residual pressure could have caused movement. If complete but design relies on hydraulics for retention, this highlights a design flaw.
questions.decisionUnlocked: If isolation was incomplete or misinterpreted, residual pressure could have caused movement. If complete but design relies on hydraulics for retention, this highlights a design flaw.

questions.text: What specific structural members or connections supported the carrier beam when work rolls were removed?
questions.rationale: Understanding load paths helps determine if gravity alone was sufficient to cause failure once hydraulic support vanished.
questions.decisionUnlocked: Understanding load paths helps determine if gravity alone was sufficient to cause failure once hydraulic support vanished.

questions.text: Did the previous shift explicitly communicate to the current team that a mechanical lock was required or already applied before leaving the balance in a raised position?
questions.rationale: The timeline mentions an 'Unobserved interval' between isolation and fall. A communication gap during handover could explain why no one verified the state of the beam.
evidenceNeeded: Shift turnover log (EV-006), Witness statements from previous shift crew.
questions.decisionUnlocked: The timeline mentions an 'Unobserved interval' between isolation and fall. A communication gap during handover could explain why no one verified the state of the beam.

questions.text: Did the previous shift explicitly communicate to Turn 2 that the Top Backup Roll Balance was left in a raised position and isolated, including any specific warnings about residual energy?

questions.decisionUnlocked: The 'unobserved interval' suggests potential communication gaps. If Turn 2 assumed isolation without verification based on incomplete handoff info.

questions.rationale: Identifies if a subsequent action (e.g., removing a pin, shifting weight) triggered the release or if it was an uncontrolled decay over time.

questions.decisionUnlocked: Identifies if a subsequent action (e.g., removing a pin, shifting weight) triggered the release or if it was an uncontrolled decay over time.
